Elderly, handicapped, those with planned travel, and certain occupations (like on-duty all-day firefighters) have access to absentee ballots in my state; and most states have similar rules. Absentee ballots have a series of checks built in. First, they must be requested. Second, before absentee ballots are issued, the registration is checked at the county elections office and the voter will not be able to easily change and vote in-person on election day (there would be extra paperwork and they'd be given a provisional ballot). Third, my state uses a double-envelope system and a witness signature on the outside of the inner sealed envelope containing the ballot is required, which is used to account for checking that the ballot returned was the one that was issued.

Those procedures are very different and far more secure than vote-by-mail which has subcontractors mail out ballots by mailing lists, entrusts the postal service with the security of delivering mass mailings, and has little-to-no mechanism for verifying that the person who filled out the ballot was the same person who was registered to vote.
